title: Nasdaq-100 Fast-Entry Rule Takes Effect
summary: The Nasdaq-100 Index's new fast-entry rule becomes operative. Large-cap IPOs with low float may now be evaluated for inclusion beginning approximately the 7th trading day after listing, with addition approximately 15 trading days after listing, subject to a $5M average daily trading volume (ADTV) liquidity test. Low-float qualifying names enter at a capped weight (approximately one-third of float-adjusted market cap or three times the float cap, whichever is lower) and ramp up at subsequent quarterly reconstitutions.

title: Russell 1000 Annual Reconstitution (June 2026)
summary: FTSE Russell conducts its annual reconstitution of the Russell 1000 and Russell 2000 indexes in June. Large IPOs that listed before the rank date (typically end of May) may be eligible for the annual reconstitution. IPOs listing after the rank cutoff must wait until the following year's reconstitution or an interim addition decision.

title: S&P DJI: No Fast-Entry Rule Adopted (Standing Policy)
summary: As of the publication date of this page, S&P Dow Jones Indices has not adopted a fast-entry rule for the S&P 500 or related indexes. S&P 500 eligibility requires: (1) U.S. company, (2) market cap above $18B (approximate threshold, confirmed in S&P 500 methodology), (3) annual positive GAAP earnings, (4) at least 12 months of trading history, (5) adequate float. A company qualifying for Nasdaq-100 fast entry would not simultaneously qualify for the S&P 500.
confidence: confirmed — per S&P 500 index methodology document
